name: D K Plastics
old_description: Family-owned and headquartered in Archer, Iowa. Founded 1995. We extruded our first HDPE sheet in 1998, in a 6,000 sq ft building. As production grew, extrusion moved into a dedicated 24,000 sq ft building; vacuum thermoforming and CNC routing run from the original shop, expanded over the years.
about:
D K Plastics is a family-owned manufacturer headquartered in Archer, Iowa. The company was founded in 1995 and extruded its first HDPE sheet in 1998, starting in a 6,000-square-foot building.

Today the operation spans three product lines: heavy-gauge HDPE sheet extrusion (.060–.750 inch thick, widths to 60 inches, rolls to 500 feet, virgin or reprocessed with an FDA food-grade option), vacuum thermoforming on a single-platen press (up to 48 by 96 inches, draw depth to 14 inches), and precision CNC routing (60 by 240 inch bed). Extrusion runs in a dedicated 24,000-square-foot facility, while thermoforming and routing operate from the original shop. The company serves prototype through production volumes.

Primary customers include marine and recreational vehicle manufacturers, with the company also offering FDA food-grade HDPE for food-contact applications.

The business emphasizes in-house extrusion and finishing, allowing control over material quality and lead times from its Iowa location.

about:
DM & P Supplies, Inc., a multi-generational family-owned business, has operated from St. Paul, Minnesota since its founding in 2005. The company was established to provide deli, meat, and produce departments with food processing equipment and supplies, drawing on the founders' combined half-century of industry experience.

The distributor stocks a broad range of merchandising and processing items, including saw blades, grinder knives and plates, cutlery, scales, vacuum bags, trays, case liners, baskets, signage, and a variety of spices, seasonings, and kits for sausage, bratwurst, and salami production. Its inventory serves both wholesale and smaller-scale producers.

Primary customers include custom processors, grocers, and meat markets across the food-processing sector. The company's vendor relationships allow it to source equipment and supplies for meat, deli, and produce departments from recognized manufacturers.

The firm emphasizes its 50-plus years of combined experience and long-standing manufacturer relationships as the basis for offering cutting-edge, quality products at affordable prices, positioning itself as a knowledgeable partner for food-service operations.

name: DBS Stainless Steel Fabricators
old_description: Established in 1985, DBS Stainless Steel Fabricators has become a trusted name in Metal Fabrication, specializing in custom stainless steel products for the Cincinnati Tri-State Area and beyond. Our range of expertise encompasses Restaurant Equipment, Industrial Parts, and Residential Countertops, ensuring we can meet the unique needs of diverse industries. DBS understands the demanding nature of the Restaurant Industry and offers a wide selection of solutions, from Chef's Counters to Wall Panels and Corner Guards, assisting our clients in creating custom and durable workspaces. With over 40 years of experience, our commitment to delivering superior quality products, and exceptional service sets us apart as the leading innovators in our field.
about:
DBS Stainless Steel Fabricators was established in 1985 in Hamilton, Ohio, serving the Cincinnati Tri-State Area with custom stainless steel fabrication. The company began as a metal fabrication shop focused on stainless steel products.

The shop specializes in custom stainless steel fabrication across three main categories: restaurant equipment, industrial parts, and residential countertops. Its capabilities include forming, welding, and finishing stainless steel into items such as chef's counters, wall panels, corner guards, bar tops, shelving, and custom residential pieces. Project records from 2016 through 2025 show work ranging from commercial bar installations to residential countertops and specialty items like copper and brass counter tops.

DBS serves the restaurant industry, industrial clients, and residential customers. Notable projects include stainless steel laundry and trash receptacles for the Cincinnati Bengals, custom countertops for the Indian Hill Residence, and custom steps for an Airstream trailer. The company also produces bar and restaurant fixtures such as pass-through counters, condiment stands, and steam counters.

The company cites its commitment to quality craftsmanship and service as what distinguishes it in the field, built on over four decades of fabrication experience.

The business grew out of DimcoGray Corporation, a long-standing producer of thermoplastic and thermoset knobs and handles, giving the team more than 30 years of plastics molding experience before the DG Medical name was adopted. The company provides molding solutions, assembly, prototyping, and packaging services for medical devices. Its molding operations use process control technology to monitor production, while prototyping includes 3-D printed models from customer designs. Packaging lines combine automated and manual processes, and engineering support covers mold design and material selection. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not publicly disclosed.

DG Medical serves medical device original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), describing its customer base as many of the world's medical device companies. Specific client names are not provided.

name: DMS Machining & Fabrication
old_description: DMS Machining is a full service machine shop serving the Northeast since 1991. Specializing in designing, building, installing industrial components and structural steel for many industries, our experienced machinists, fabricators and MSHA Certified field crew can deploy assets to meet your every need.
about:
DMS Machining & Fabrication was founded in 1991 in Barre, Vermont. The company is led by President/Owner Byron Atwood, who has been with the firm since its inception, alongside Operations Manager & Owner Charlie Atwood and Office Administration Diane Atwood. The business began with a mission to deliver quality work on time and at a fair price, serving industrial, commercial, and construction customers across the Northeast.

Operating from a 45,000‑square‑foot facility on three acres just off I‑89, the shop houses a 40,000‑square‑foot main production area spanned by eight bridge cranes, plus a 5,000‑square‑foot “Roadhouse” for field‑service deployment. The equipment roster includes a range of manual and CNC lathes (Southbend, Southwestern, Poreba, Okuma, Monarch), vertical turret lathes (Bullard), milling machines (Bridgeport, Southwestern CNC, Cincinnati, Futurmill), horizontal boring mills (Wotan, G&L), a Morrison keyseater, and an Eutectic Terodyn thermal‑spray system. The company performs machining, steel and metal fabrication, mechanical repair, design and engineering, and on‑site field services, with rare need for outsourcing.

DMS serves mining, energy (hydropower, biomass), construction, manufacturing, aggregate, asphalt, wood products, educational institutions, hospitals, and ski resorts throughout the Northeast. Its MSHA‑certified field crew travels in fully equipped trucks to handle emergency repairs, planned maintenance, and new installations at customer sites.

The firm emphasizes its enduring commitment to “quality work delivered on time and at a fair price,” backed by continuous investment in skilled personnel, equipment, and stringent safety protocols. This focus has built a reputation for completing complex projects that require both shop‑based precision and on‑site adaptability.

Projects have ranged from a replacement grill grease catcher to full commercial kitchen build-outs and artistic installations such as a large-scale United States map display.

The company emphasizes integrity, quality craftsmanship, innovation, and customer satisfaction as core values, aiming to deliver attention to detail and reliable service on every job.

name: DairyChem
old_description: DairyChem includes two divisions that support and expand our flavor capabilities. Ingretec, a sister company owned by DairyChem, specializes in cheese flavorings and fillings. FLVRtec, a subsidiary developed by DairyChem, produces natural compound liquid flavors used across a variety of applications
about:
DairyChem is headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, and has been manufacturing natural dairy flavors since 1933. The family-owned company traces its origins to Dr. Leon Chumlea, who developed a signature dairy flavor by guiding milk fermentation and distilling the most impactful flavor notes. DairyChem later acquired Chumlea's laboratory and expanded its capabilities and product portfolio.

Today, DairyChem produces dairy concentrates, natural flavors, and clean-label solutions in a modern manufacturing plant. Its core processes include fermentation, steam distillation, and natural enzyme modification of milk, butter, and cheese. The company also offers blended and compounded flavor systems in liquid, paste, or spray-dried powder forms. Two divisions extend its reach: Ingretec, a sister company specializing in cheese flavorings and fillings that are two to six times stronger than conventional cheese, and FLVRtec, a subsidiary creating natural, allergen-free liquid flavors for savory, sweet, and emerging categories.

DairyChem serves food and beverage manufacturers across applications such as sauces, fillings, soups, spreads, dips, dressings, processed cheese, and dairy alternatives. Its customers rely on the company for flavor enhancement, cost savings, fat reduction, and consistency in products ranging from snack foods to dairy-based beverages.

As a family-owned, independent business, DairyChem emphasizes long-term partnership, short lead times, custom packaging, and flexible ordering. Its R&D team combines deep dairy expertise with modern food science to deliver stable, versatile flavors that perform in real-world processing conditions.

name: Dakota Metal Solutions LLC
old_description: Dakota Metal Solutions LLC is a high-precision metal fabrication and automated contract manufacturing company based in Summit, South Dakota, serving OEMs across the Upper Midwest. Equipped with advanced Bystronic 6kW/8kW fiber lasers, automated TRUMPF press brakes, Okuma CNC machining centers, and integrated multi-axis robotic welding cells, Dakota Metal Solutions specializes in scalable, lights-out production for sheet metal, tube, and heavy plate up to 1 inch thick. From collaborative DFM engineering and custom fixture fabrication to structural weldments and turnkey assembly, the company delivers exceptional repeatability, tight tolerances, and cost-effective OEM manufacturing solutions.
about:
Dakota Metal Solutions LLC operates from a 96,800-square-foot facility in Summit, South Dakota. The company was founded in 2021 with the goal of building a fabrication shop designed for modern manufacturing, combining advanced equipment with efficient production processes.

The shop specializes in high-precision metal fabrication and automated contract manufacturing for OEMs. Its capabilities span fiber laser cutting (sheet up to 5×10 feet, 28 gauge to 1 inch thick), tube laser cutting, CNC milling and turning, automated press brake forming, multi-axis robotic welding, and flat finishing. The facility houses more than 20 advanced machines, including Bystronic 6 kW and 8 kW fiber lasers, a TRUMPF automated press brake, Okuma and Doosan machining centers, and integrated robotic welding cells. An ERP system manages production scheduling and assembly integration, supporting scalable, lights-out production runs.

Dakota Metal Solutions serves OEMs across the Upper Midwest, with delivery throughout North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Wyoming, Minnesota, Iowa, and Nebraska. Key industries include agricultural machinery, heavy industrial equipment, construction equipment, truck and trailer manufacturing, and general industrial OEMs. The company produces precision sheet metal components, structural weldments, laser-cut brackets and enclosures, CNC-machined parts, and heavy-equipment sub-assemblies, as well as its own line of steel products such as chip hoppers and hose holders.

The company differentiates itself by engineering the production process—not just the part—through custom fixtures, workholding systems, and in-house automation like the Corsink Pro™ multi-hole drilling system. This approach aims to reduce secondary operations, minimize manual handling, and improve output reliability for repeat production programs.

name: Dane Manufacturing
old_description: Whether you need us for metal fabrication or contract manufacturing expertise, we’ll use our innovative processes, experienced staff and our state-of-the-art facility to deliver manufacturing services you can trust.
about:
Dane Manufacturing operates from Waunakee, Wisconsin, where it was established in 1917 by a group of local investors to produce a below‑the‑frost‑line water pump. The company’s early success came with the Can’t Clog hog feeder, a staple in agriculture, before it transitioned into contract manufacturing. In 2001, engineer and CEO Troy Berg acquired the business, steering it toward innovation while retaining a focus on employee development and customer service.

Today the firm provides end‑to‑end metal fabrication and contract manufacturing services, including laser cutting, forming, welding, assembly and integration, packaging, order fulfillment, and finishing. Technical support covers process planning and material selection. Quality control relies on an InspecVision Planar P220.35 high‑speed 2D measurement system alongside staff inspections. Production takes place in a 510,000‑square‑foot smart factory that incorporates automated equipment and streamlined operations.

Dane primarily serves OEM manufacturers across various sectors, drawing on a history that includes agricultural equipment. The company positions itself as a partner that handles projects from initial design through final delivery, offering logistics support such as packaging and shipping.

The company’s stated mission is to enrich employees, customers, and the community through entrepreneurial spirit and innovative metal solutions. Core values — Invest, Innovate, Integrity, Excellence — guide its operations. Dane highlights its ISO 9001:2015 certification, six INC 5000 awards (2007, 2008, 2009, 2013, 2019, 2020), and a culture of continuous capability expansion as key differentiators.
